cases.question: How do sliding-mode controllers reduce chattering in motor drives?

expected_refs.snippet: Sliding-Mode Control Strategies for PMSM speed control
Disturbance Observer-Based Chattering-Attenuated Terminal Sliding Mode Control

cases.fixture_answer: Chattering reduction should be explained as a design tradeoff, with PMSM SMC taxonomy context [1] and disturbance-observer terminal SMC evidence [2].
cases.recorded_answer: Sliding-mode controllers reduce chattering by treating switching gain, boundary layers, and disturbance-observer compensation as design tradeoffs. For PMSM control, the review frames chattering reduction as a core SMC research concern [1]. Chattering-attenuated terminal SMC then combines disturbance observation with terminal sliding surfaces to reduce switching ripple while preserving robustness [2].

cases.question: Explain why increasing terminal SMC switching gain can reduce tracking error but worsen chattering.

expected_refs.snippet: Disturbance Observer-Based Chattering-Attenuated Terminal Sliding Mode Control

cases.fixture_answer: The answer should explain the gain/chattering tradeoff using the chattering-attenuated terminal SMC and disturbance-observer context [1].
cases.recorded_answer: Increasing terminal SMC switching gain can improve robustness against disturbance and reduce tracking error, but excessive gain injects high-frequency switching that appears as chattering. A chattering-attenuated terminal SMC design uses disturbance-observer compensation to reduce that tradeoff rather than only raising gain [1].
